comments.body: I always wish I can find something to quibble with but I cant. While it isnt just one issue, the retirement age of 62 is ridiculous and this is a powerful variable. would love to see the projections if moved to 65? And 65 is not old when LE is 80.

children.name: Jon
children.body: The problem is that biological ageing accelerates after 60 and this fact is amplified in people's minds by the media to the point where it's assumed that in your 70's you'll be battling ill-health and fending off the Reaper. Add to that a previous generation where the middle classes often retired in their mid-50's and the demand for earlier retirement is working in the opposite direction to our fiscal requirements.

children.name: Impossible Santa Wife
children.body:
The other big problem, at least in the US, is ageism. If nobody wants to *hire* older people or keep them on at a company, they might wind up retiring when in fact they still want to work. And then we hear younger people howling about how “Boomers” are “clogging the pipeline.”

We can make it easier for older people to work (and pay taxes) OR we can spend a ton of money on old age entitlements. We can’t simultaneously deny older people jobs and then complain about how much of our budget is eaten

children.name: Jon
children.body:
Absolutely. Society can't fret about an adverse ratio of older-retired to younger-working people and then deny working opportunities to older people. Even if we do insist on working from home, keeping a lot of medical appointments and slowing down meetings with irrelevant ponderings.

But AI's not a problem. When you've spent much of your working life having to use technical books to learn things and google searches to find out facts, using AI is like having superpowers.
